_README.description: Master data file for the Chereskin Lab ADCP Data Portal. Edit this file to update all site content. Then run 'python3 -m http.server 8000' and open localhost:8000 to preview changes.
_README.image_paths: All image filenames in cruise.images[] are relative to the images/ folder. Example: 'nh9310_100_oa.jpg' → place file at images/nh9310_100_oa.jpg
_README.branding_note: project.logo, project.header_image and project.illustration_image are relative to the images/ folder (harvested from the original adcp.ucsd.edu under images/branding/). logo appears on the overview project card and the project page hero; header_image is the project hero banner photo (paired with header_credit); illustration_image sits beside the project page's Acknowledgments panel (paired with illustration_credit). All are optional — omit them to fall back to the plain card/hero layout.
_README.track_format: cruise.track is an optional array of [latitude, longitude] pairs used only when no measured track exists in data/drake_passage_tracks.json.
_README.station_format: cruise.stations is an array of {lat, lon, label} objects for individual station markers on the map.
_README.ncei_url_note: cruise.ncei_url is the permanent NCEI accession landing page: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/archive/accession/XXXXXXX . For 1999–2018 the JASADCP submissions were archived in batches, so many cruises share one accession; cruise.ncei_accession holds the bare number.
_README.contact: Chereskin Lab, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UCSD
_README.tracks_file: data/drake_passage_tracks.json holds the measured ship tracks (ensembles with valid u and v) and the per-depth-bin data-coverage statistics extracted from the CODAS databases with pysadcp. A cruise is linked to its track through cruise.track_key. Regenerate it with make_drake_passage_web_tracks.py (kept outside this repository, it needs pycurrents/CODAS and the raw loads): the 2019-onwards cruises come from the UHDAS loads under drake_passage_2019_onwards/, and the 1999–2018 cruises from the JAS-ADCP repository, selected with select_drake_passage_jas_dbs.py and merged in with --db-list / --merge-into.
_README.antarctic_webpy_gallery_file: data/antarctic_webpy_gallery.json is the generated manifest for standard pycurrents/CODAS PNG figures selected with an Antarctic cruise's Plots button. It is deliberately separate from cruise.images[]; make_drake_passage_web_gallery.py (kept beside the CODAS science tools) copies existing recent webpy output or renders source databases offline into scratch, then publishes only static PNGs and thumbnails under images/antarctic-webpy/.
_README.jasadcp_note: cruise.sac_id is the JASADCP (NODC/UH SAC) cruise id of the cruise's primary database, and cruise.jasadcp_url is its page at https://uhslc.soest.hawaii.edu/sadcp/DATABASE/<sac_id>.html . A cruise that submitted more than one sonar has one SAC id per database; they are all listed in cruise.sac_ids[] as {sac_id, sonar}, and the same ids appear per instrument in data/drake_passage_tracks.json.

projects.name: Antarctic — Laurence M. Gould
projects.vessel: ARSV Laurence M. Gould & RVIB Nathaniel B. Palmer
projects.illustration_credit: LMG ADCP program sticker, Chereskin Lab
projects.description: Shipboard ADCP data from the Drake Passage time series, run by the Chereskin group since the hull-mounted 150 kHz narrowband RDI instrument was installed on the ARSV Laurence M. Gould in September 1999. Almost every Gould crossing of Drake Passage and transit along the western Antarctic Peninsula has been measured since; a 38 kHz Ocean Surveyor was added in November 2004, roughly tripling the profiling range. Five cDrake cruises aboard the RVIB Nathaniel B. Palmer (2007–2011) are included. The 1999–2018 cruises are the science-ready sets submitted to the Joint Archive for Shipboard ADCP (JASADCP) and archived at NCEI; 2019 onwards are processed in house.
projects.methods_text: Data processed using CODAS3 with standard heading calibration procedures. Bottom tracking was available for shallow transits near the Peninsula. Navigation corrections applied via differential GPS.
projects.acknowledgments: The collection, processing and dissemination of these data was carried out by the Chereskin Lab at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UCSD with support from NSF awards 9816226, 0338103, 0838750, 1341431, 1542902, and 2001646. Eric Firing and Jules Hummon at the University of Hawaii provide critical support for the data acquisition and processing of these ADCP data through the development and maintenance of the UHDAS and CODAS software.

projects.description: A decade of shipboard ADCP measurements of upper ocean currents off Southern and Central California as part of the quarterly California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) cruises.
projects.methods_text: Data collected with RDI 150 kHz narrowband instrument, hull-mounted aboard R/V New Horizon. Processed with CODAS3. Objective mapping applied to produce velocity streamfunctions consistent with geostrophy.
projects.acknowledgments: The CalCOFI ADCP data were collected aboard R/V New Horizon as part of the California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations program. The collection, processing and dissemination of these data was carried out by the Chereskin Lab at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UCSD with support from NSF award 0324360. The data are archived and distributed through the Joint Archive for Shipboard ADCP at the University of Hawaii and NOAA/NCEI.
references: Chereskin, T.K. and Trunnell, M. (1996). Correlation scales, objective mapping, and absolute geostrophic velocity in the California Current. J. Geophys. Res., 101(C10), 22619–22629.
